clues: This town sits south of Quito, the chief city of Ecuador. A ring of volcanoes stands all round it.
The days stay mild all year, with highs near nineteen and lows near ten. The dry months come in June, July, and August.
Humboldt named this land the Avenue of Volcanoes. Eight volcanoes stand in its wide valley.
Its ground gives out warm spring water all year long. One valley near by has twenty two springs, and folks prize their healing touch.
This town owns part of one great live volcano, Cotopaxi. That huge peak is the crown of its ring of fire hills.
